why: The error codes a host exposes are the last vocabulary crossing the engine boundary
with nothing behind it. Every other shared name in this repository is generated or
gated: field types, function aliases, the runtime projection, the runtime versions,
the shared bounds, the structural rules, the event kinds, even the preset facade's
method list. Error codes were not.
What the boundary actually carries is `@errorName(err)` -- see `runtimeError` in
packages/zig/wasm/src/abi.zig -- so a host code that names an engine error is
coupled to the spelling of a Zig error, and nothing said so. Rename the error and
the host keeps matching a string the engine no longer produces: no compile error, no
test failure, just a code that stops arriving. `scene-safe.ts` then falls through to
a plain Error and the caller loses the code it was switching on.
So every code in the gated host unions is classified here.
shared    -- the host code is an engine error name, spelled identically.
renamed   -- the host deliberately re-words an engine error. The mapping has to
exist in scene-safe.ts, and this file is where the pair is recorded.
hostOnly  -- the host raises it itself; the engine has no such error.
vestigial -- nothing can currently raise it. Kept in the exported union, recorded
here so it is a decision rather than a leftover.
A code in none of the four fails the gate, and so does a `shared` or `renamed` code
whose engine error no longer exists.
Found on the first run: six codes in the vestigial list below. They date from when
TypeScript executed scenes itself; the engine took that over and the vocabulary was
never trimmed. They are exported types no code path can produce, which is what this
gate exists to stop happening again.

ungatedUnions.RunnerErrorCode: the host's own API misuse vocabulary; no engine error corresponds
ungatedUnions.ModelValidationErrorCode: why a model was rejected, decided by the host from the engine's status

shared.why: a prog named a preset the engine does not have
two actions in one scene share an id
a publish hook failed under failOnPublishError
the scene declares no entry action
a prepare hook the action names is not registered
an extend hook the action names is not registered
a prepare hook omitted a binding it owes
an action referenced a binding it never produced
a write targeted a reserved STATE path
a read or write targeted an undeclared STATE path
a value did not match the type the schema declares
a STATE field declares a type the engine cannot parse
a literal in the model is not a value the engine accepts

renamed.why: the host reports the action a caller named, not the engine's lookup failure
a scene reached through an action reference reads to the caller as a bad action

hostOnly.why: result() was called before the run finished; the engine was never asked
the host validates what a hook returned before the engine ever sees it
state-manager.ts bounds nesting before encoding for the boundary

route-safe.ts raises it when the entry scene is absent from the map the caller passed, before the engine is reached. It was vestigial while that path threw a bare Error; the engine's own lookup failure is SceneNotFound, classified under renamed

vestigial.why: from the TypeScript executor; the engine rejects a malformed ArgModel at load
from the TypeScript executor; the engine lowers bindings in dependency order
from the TypeScript executor; no current path raises it
from the TypeScript executor; structure.zig itemises this at model load
from the TypeScript executor. turnout-runtime's builder has its own code of this name, which is a separate vocabulary and not gated here
from the TypeScript prepare phase; the engine resolves from_state itself
